title: Google adds a User Alignment Critic and origin isolation to Gemini agentic browsing in Chrome
summary: On 8 December 2025 Google engineer Nathan Parker described a layered security architecture for the Gemini-powered agentic browsing features planned for Chrome, combining deterministic rules, model-level protections, isolation boundaries and user oversight to mitigate indirect prompt injection from page content. A User Alignment Critic, a separate model isolated from untrusted content and treated as a high-trust system component, vets every action the primary agent proposes and orders a retry or returns control to the user when an action is risky or irrelevant to the user's goal; Origin Sets limit the agent to specific sites and elements, withhold unrelated origins and iframes, and require a trusted gating function to approve new origins; a dedicated classifier scans pages for indirect prompt injection alongside Safe Browsing; Chrome pauses for manual confirmation on sensitive sites such as banking portals or Password Manager sign-ins; and Google backs the design with automated red-teaming and bounties of up to $20,000 for breaking it.
verification_note: URL fetched 2026-10-17; BleepingComputer article by Bill Toulas dated December 8, 2025. Confirmed from the page text: Google engineer Nathan Parker announced a layered architecture for Gemini agentic browsing in Chrome; the User Alignment Critic is a separate model isolated from untrusted content, acting as a high-trust system component, that vets each proposed action and orders a retry or returns control to the user if the action is risky or irrelevant to the user's goal; Origin Sets withhold unrelated origins including iframes and a trusted gating function must approve new origins; manual confirmation on sensitive sites such as banking portals and Password Manager sign-ins; a dedicated indirect-prompt-injection classifier running alongside Safe Browsing; automated red-teaming and bounties of up to $20,000. All candidate claims matched; the page also names the injection classifier and red-teaming, now included in the summary. Gemini has been integrated into Chrome since September 2025 per the article.
